h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Alcoa, TN
hero_subtitle: From the original company-town streets near Springbrook Park to new construction at Springbrook Farm, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed Alcoa roofers. Free, with no obligation.
intro: Alcoa is one of the few places in East Tennessee where a roofer can spend the morning on a house the Aluminum Company of America built for its plant workers around 1920 and the afternoon on one finished in the last few years. The city was chartered in 1919 as a planned company town, and its four original sections, Vose, Springbrook, Bassel and Hall, still define the older neighborhoods. Tell us about your roof and you can compare quotes from up to three licensed, insured local roofers.

sections.heading: Company-town houses that are now a century old
body: ALCOA bought the land in 1910, began its South Plant in 1913 and started building the town site in 1917. Company engineers laid out four sections: Vose and Springbrook in the north, around what is now Springbrook Park, and Bassel and Hall in the south near the South Plant. The company built hundreds of houses for its workers, then sold them off beginning in the early 1950s, mostly to the families who lived in them.

Seventy-some years of private ownership means no two of those houses share the same roof history. Some have been re-roofed several times, and on houses this age it is common to find a newer layer of shingles nailed over an older one. If you own one, ask each roofer what they expect to find underneath, whether their price covers a full tear-off down to the deck, and how they will handle plank sheathing that may be original to the house.

sections.heading: Springbrook Farm and Alcoa's newer housing
body: The other side of Alcoa is brand new. Springbrook Farm, a mixed-use development on the roughly 360-acre site of the former ALCOA West Plant, broke ground in 2017 and has been adding shops, apartments, offices and land planned for single-family homes and townhomes. It sits beside the Maryville Alcoa Greenway, which runs through Springbrook Park on its way to Hunt Road.

Newer roofs come with paperwork worth finding before you call anyone. Pull out the builder's closing documents and the shingle manufacturer's warranty, because a roofer may need to know who installed the original roof and which product line was used in order to keep that coverage intact. Also check any neighborhood covenants that limit shingle colors or materials.

sections.heading: Homes, shops and city limits
body: Alcoa packs a lot of commercial property into a small city, from shopping centers like Hamilton Crossing at West Bessemer Street and Alcoa Highway to businesses along Hall Road and near McGhee Tyson Airport. If you own a shop, office or rental building with a low-slope roof, say so on the form so you are matched with contractors who handle that type of roof.

City limits and mailing addresses do not line up neatly here. Alcoa lies partly in ZIP codes shared with Maryville and Louisville, so an address alone will not tell a roofer whether the City of Alcoa or Blount County handles a permit. Confirm which side of the line you are on, then ask the roofer whether your job needs one.

Spring and summer thunderstorms are the usual source of sudden roof damage in Blount County. After a storm, take your time, be wary of door-to-door offers and compare written estimates that spell out tear-off, underlayment, flashing and ventilation.

roofing_notes: Original company houses may hide more than one shingle layer and plank decking; get tear-off and decking prices in writing.
Ask how ventilation will be handled on older homes built long before ridge vents were standard.
On newer Springbrook Farm homes, have builder and shingle warranty documents ready before getting quotes.
Confirm whether your property is inside Alcoa city limits or in Blount County before asking about permits.

faqs.q: My house is one of the original ALCOA company homes. Does that change the roof job?
faqs.a: It can. Those houses date to the company's building program around 1917 to 1920, and a century of repairs means a roofer may find more than one layer of shingles or original plank decking underneath. Neither is unusual, but both affect cost. Ask every roofer to quote a full tear-off, explain how they price damaged decking, and put that unit price in writing before work starts.

faqs.q: My Springbrook Farm home is only a few years old. Why would I need roofing quotes?
faqs.a: Newer roofs are not immune to wind, hail or installation problems. If something looks wrong, check the builder's warranty and the shingle manufacturer's coverage first, then get an independent inspection. Written assessments from more than one roofer help you tell a storm claim from a minor repair, and give you something concrete to show your builder or insurer.

faqs.q: Can I get quotes for a commercial or rental property in Alcoa?
faqs.a: Yes. Alcoa has plenty of commercial property along Alcoa Highway and Hall Road, and many roofing contractors handle low-slope systems as well as shingles. Describe the building, the roof type and its rough size on the form so you are matched with roofers who do that kind of work. The service is free and you are under no obligation to hire anyone.

name: Seymour
title: Seymour, TN Roofing Quotes | Sevier & Blount Roofers
meta_description: Get free roofing quotes in Seymour, TN. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers serving both the Sevier and Blount County sides of Seymour. No obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Seymour, TN
hero_subtitle: Whether your home is off Chapman Highway, Boyds Creek Highway or a back road facing Bluff Mountain, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed Seymour-area roofers at no cost.
intro: Seymour is a community of nearly 15,000 people with no city government. It straddles the northwest corner of Sevier County and the northeast corner of Blount County, and when incorporation has come up, voters have chosen to stay unincorporated. That makes the county line more than a map detail when you need a roof replaced. Many homes look toward Bluff Mountain and the Chilhowee ridge, which is part of the appeal and part of the roofing challenge. Request quotes and compare up to three licensed, insured roofers.

sections.heading: One community, two counties
body: Seymour has always been a crossroads. It began as Newell's Station, a frontier post founded in 1783 where Sevier County's first court met in 1785, was known as Trundles Crossroads in the 1800s, and took its current name from Charles Seymour, chief engineer of the Knoxville, Sevierville and Eastern Railway, which arrived in 1909. The center of the community is still a junction, where Chapman Highway, US 411 from Maryville and Boyds Creek Highway meet.

Because Seymour is unincorporated, there is no town hall to call about building questions. Depending on which side of the line your house sits, the county offices in Sevierville or Maryville are the ones that matter, and your property tax bill is the quickest way to check. A roofer who works here regularly will ask about this before planning the job.

sections.heading: Mountain views and wind exposure
body: Seymour sits between Bays Mountain to the north and Bluff Mountain, the northern end of Chilhowee Mountain, to the south. If your home sits on a rise or an open former field to take in that view, its roof also catches more of the gusty wind that comes with spring and summer thunderstorms.

On an exposed roof, ask each roofer for the shingle's wind rating, how many nails they use per shingle and how they secure the starter course along the eaves and rakes, where wind uplift usually begins. If you are weighing metal against architectural shingles, ask for both to be priced on the same quote so the comparison is fair.

sections.heading: A growing Chapman Highway corridor
body: Chapman Highway has been widened in stages through Seymour. The section from Foothills Drive toward Sevierville was finished in 2016, and the stretch from Macon Lane to Boyds Creek Highway was completed in 2023. A state-funded study of Boyds Creek Highway between Chapman Highway and Old Knoxville Highway has recommended more lanes and signals as traffic grows.

That growth leaves Seymour with newer subdivision homes near the main roads alongside older houses on roads like Burnett Station Road and Simmons Road. On older homes, chimney flashing and roof-to-wall joints are frequent leak points, so ask whether new flashing is included in the price or billed as an extra.

roofing_notes: Check your property tax bill to confirm whether your home is in Sevier or Blount County before discussing permits.
Homes on open lots facing Bluff Mountain take more wind; ask about wind-rated shingles and the nailing pattern.
Ask whether chimney and wall flashing replacement is included, especially on older homes off the main roads.
If you are deciding between metal and shingles, have both priced on the same quote.

faqs.q: Does it matter whether my Seymour home is in Sevier County or Blount County?
faqs.a: It can. Seymour has no city government, so building questions go to the county your home is in rather than a town office. Your property tax bill shows which county that is. Roofers matched with you through this service work in the 37865 ZIP code on both sides of the line, but telling them your county up front helps them plan the job and check any local requirements.

faqs.q: Will roofers from Knoxville, Maryville or Sevierville come out to Seymour?
faqs.a: Seymour sits on Chapman Highway between Knoxville and Sevierville, and US 411 connects it to Maryville, so it is an easy drive for contractors based in any of them. You can be matched with up to three licensed, insured roofers who cover Seymour, and they usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours. Comparing their quotes costs you nothing.

faqs.q: My house faces the mountains and catches a lot of wind. What should I ask for?
faqs.a: Ask each roofer which shingle wind rating they plan to use, whether they follow the manufacturer's high-wind nailing pattern, and how they seal the starter strip and ridge cap. Those details decide whether shingles stay put in a strong thunderstorm gust. Compare the answers side by side; a quote that skips them is harder to judge, even if the price is lower.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Karns, TN
hero_subtitle: From long-established homes along Oak Ridge Highway to new subdivisions off Karns Valley Drive, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed roofers serving Karns and the 37931 ZIP code.
intro: Karns sits in the Beaver Creek valley in northwest Knox County, between Beaver Ridge and Copper Ridge, about 11 miles from downtown Knoxville. The community was called Beaver Ridge until residents voted in the 1950s to take the name of Karns High School, which opened in 1913. For most of its history this was farm country. Today pastures, older homes on the main roads and a steady run of new subdivisions share the valley, and Karns roofs span every one of those eras.

sections.heading: From farm valley to growth corridor
body: Karns has shifted from mostly farming to a mix of subdivisions, small businesses and schools, and road projects have sped that up. Karns Valley Drive was connected to the Hardin Valley area in 2017, and county planners have pointed to significant residential development along it since. The long-running Schaad Road extension, which a 2019 report said serves Ball Camp, Byington, Karns and scores of subdivisions in between, has opened up more land.

The result is a wide spread of roof ages along the same few miles of road. Subdivisions such as Walkers Gate and Brookhaven were finished years ago, while Emory Green and the Archstone condominiums were still under construction in 2024. One Karns homeowner may be pricing a second or third roof while a neighbor across the road is still on the builder's original.

sections.heading: Beaver Creek, ridges and sinkholes
body: This is classic Ridge-and-Valley country. Knox County planning reports for Karns sites regularly flag Beaver Creek floodplain, steep slopes, tree canopy worth preserving, and closed depressions that can signal sinkholes. Beaver Creek itself is now a county water trail, with a kayak launch at the Knox County Sportspark next to the Karns Senior Center.

That terrain shows up on roofs in a few ways. Homes high on the slopes of Beaver Ridge or Copper Ridge are more open to wind, while houses on wooded lots get more shade, leaf litter and moss. Gutters matter here too: on low ground near the creek, water that pours off a roof edge and pools against the foundation turns into a crawlspace or basement problem, so ask roofers to quote gutter and downspout work alongside the roof.

sections.heading: What to ask a Karns roofer
body: On an older home, ask how the roofer will judge the decking once the old shingles are off, and get a written price for replacing damaged sheets or boards. On a newer subdivision home, find out whether your homeowners association restricts shingle colors or styles before you sign.

Karns homes carry Knoxville mailing addresses, but the community itself is unincorporated Knox County rather than part of the City of Knoxville. Mention your street address when you request quotes so contractors know which office handles any permit questions for your property.

roofing_notes: Roofs of every age sit side by side in Karns; ask for a decking assessment on older homes and keep warranties handy on newer ones.
Wooded lots near Beaver Creek collect leaves and moss; ask about gutter guards and algae-resistant shingles.
Homes on the Beaver Ridge or Copper Ridge slopes see more wind; ask about wind-rated installation.
Check homeowners association rules in newer subdivisions before choosing a shingle color.

faqs.q: Is Karns part of the City of Knoxville?
faqs.a: No. Karns is an unincorporated community in Knox County, even though homes here use Knoxville mailing addresses and the 37931 ZIP code. That means county offices, not city ones, handle building matters for most properties. Include your street address when you request quotes so the roofers matched with you can confirm the right jurisdiction and plan the job accordingly.

faqs.q: My Karns subdivision home is only a few years old. Why is the roof already giving trouble?
faqs.a: Newer roofs can still suffer from installation shortcuts, storm damage or poor attic ventilation. Before paying for repairs, check whether your builder's workmanship warranty or the shingle manufacturer's warranty still applies. An inspection from an independent roofer gives you a written second opinion you can take back to the builder or your insurer if needed.

faqs.q: Should I think about drainage near Beaver Creek when I replace my roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Your roof and gutters decide where rainwater lands. Parts of the Beaver Creek valley are mapped floodplain, and on low ground, water dumped at the foundation adds to drainage trouble. When you compare quotes, ask whether gutters, downspouts and extensions are included, and whether the roofer will check that water is carried well away from the house.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Hardin Valley, TN
hero_subtitle: Hardin Valley's subdivisions went up fast, and many of their roofs are aging together. Compare up to 3 quotes from licensed roofers who work in the 37932 area. Free, no obligation.
intro: Hardin Valley has been the fastest-growing part of Knox County since the late 2000s. Census tracts covering its core, from Yarnell Road to the Clinch River, went from 6,560 residents in 2010 to 11,101 in 2020, and the rolling farmland along Hardin Valley Road is now mostly subdivisions. That sets it apart from older parts of the Knoxville area: most homes are fairly recent, many share a builder and a homeowners association, and whole streets of roofs went on within a few years of each other.

sections.heading: A community built in a hurry
body: Hardin Valley counted about 4,750 residents in 1990 and 10,450 in 2010. Pellissippi State Community College opened its Hardin Valley campus in 1986, Hardin Valley Academy followed in 2008, and since mid-2014 more than 1,200 building permits have been issued in the area, mostly for subdivisions and apartment complexes.

Neighborhoods such as Covered Bridge, Hayden Farms and The Haven at Hardin Valley show the pattern: planned streets, amenity areas, homeowners associations and, in some of them, new homes still going up. When most of the houses on a street were roofed in the same few years, they tend to need attention around the same time too, which is worth knowing before a busy storm season.

sections.heading: HOAs, builders and warranties
body: Many Hardin Valley subdivisions have homeowners associations, and some set rules on exterior materials and colors. Before you sign a roofing contract, get your association's architectural guidelines and find out whether a replacement needs approval. A roofer can help you pick a shingle line and color that fits those rules, but submitting the request is up to you.

If your home is fairly new, read the builder's warranty and the shingle manufacturer's warranty before calling anyone. Some manufacturer warranties depend on registration or on a certified installer, so ask whether a repair or replacement will change the coverage you already have.

sections.heading: Sun, wind and former pasture
body: Hardin Valley sits at roughly 840 feet in rolling ground between Oak Ridge Highway and the Clinch River. Because much of it was built on former farmland, plenty of roofs here get full sun and open wind rather than shade from old trees.

Full sun ages shingles faster and makes attic ventilation more important, so ask each roofer to check intake and exhaust vents and explain anything they would change. After hail or high wind, many homes on one street can be hit at once and local contractors book up quickly. Lining up a few quotes early lets you compare them on your own schedule instead of taking the first crew available.

roofing_notes: Get your HOA's architectural guidelines before choosing shingles; color or material changes may need approval.
Keep builder and manufacturer warranty documents ready, and ask how a repair or replacement affects coverage.
Roofs on former pastureland get full sun; ask roofers to check attic intake and exhaust ventilation.
When a storm hits a whole subdivision, schedule an inspection promptly and compare written estimates.

faqs.q: Do I need HOA approval to replace my roof in Hardin Valley?
faqs.a: It depends on your subdivision. Many Hardin Valley neighborhoods have homeowners associations, and some require approval for changes to exterior materials or colors, even when the new roof looks similar to the old one. Ask your association or its management company for the current guidelines before you sign anything. Roofers can usually supply product names and color samples to include with an application.

faqs.q: My home was built in the last 10 years. Is it too early to need a new roof?
faqs.a: Usually a roof that young needs a repair rather than a replacement, unless a storm has damaged it. Check your builder's workmanship warranty and the shingle manufacturer's warranty first, since either may cover defects. If you are not sure whether damage came from weather or installation, a written inspection from an independent roofer gives you something to show your builder or insurer.

faqs.q: Why do so many houses on my street need roofs at the same time?
faqs.a: In Hardin Valley, entire streets were often built within a few years, so their roofs share the same age, the same exposure and sometimes the same products. When hail or high wind moves through, it tends to damage them together as well. That is a good reason to get quotes early rather than waiting for the first available crew after a storm.

name: Fountain City
title: Fountain City Roofing Quotes | North Knoxville Roofers
meta_description: Free roofing quotes in Fountain City, Knoxville. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers for bungalows, older homes and hillside lots. No obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Fountain City
hero_subtitle: From Craftsman bungalows on Gibbs Drive to older homes along Tazewell Pike and lots below Black Oak Ridge, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed Fountain City roofers. Free, no obligation.
intro: Fountain City began as a resort, not a suburb. Visitors came in the 1880s for the spring at the foot of Black Oak Ridge that forms the head of First Creek, and the heart-shaped Duck Pond in Fountain City Park is what remains of the old Fountain Head Hotel. The community stayed independent until Knoxville annexed it in 1962. Today it is a residential area tucked between Black Oak Ridge and Sharp's Ridge, with houses from the Victorian era, the 1920s bungalow years and the decades after World War II.

sections.heading: Bungalows, Victorians and post-war homes
body: The Gibbs Drive Historic District, listed on the National Register in 2000, includes 52 houses, mostly bungalows, Craftsman homes, foursquares and Minimal Traditional houses built before 1930, with some infill as late as 1950. Along Tazewell Pike, a city conservation district takes in houses from about 1860 to the 1960s, ranging from Federal and Queen Anne to Craftsman, Revival and Ranch styles.

Those houses rarely have simple roofs. The Tazewell Pike guidelines describe offset gables, telescoping gables and dormers as typical, and bungalows usually add wide eaves and a porch roof tied into the main roof. Every valley, dormer wall and porch joint needs careful flashing, so ask each roofer how they will handle them and whether the old metal is being replaced or reused.

sections.heading: What historic status means for your roof
body: National Register listing, as on Gibbs Drive, recognizes a place's history but does not by itself require design review when a private owner replaces a roof. The Tazewell Pike Neighborhood Conservation District does have local guidelines, but they cover additions, new buildings and demolition. Those guidelines state that roofing, siding, painting and similar work do not need Knoxville Historic Zoning Commission approval, even when a building permit is required.

That leaves owners plenty of flexibility. If you want the new roof to suit an older house, ask roofers to show you dimensional shingles in muted colors, and ask what they would do to protect original details such as exposed rafter tails or decorative trim at the eaves.

sections.heading: Ridges, slopes and old shade trees
body: Fountain City is framed by its ridges, Black Oak Ridge on the north and Sharp's Ridge on the south, and the ground between them is irregular enough that some houses are hard to see from the street. Along Tazewell Pike, homes sit on spacious lots set well back from the road and framed by shade trees.

Mature trees mean leaves in the gutters, moss on shaded roof faces and limbs that come down in storms. Before a replacement, ask the roofer whether branches should be trimmed back from the roof and whether they recommend gutter guards. On steep or hard-to-reach lots, ask how they will stage materials and protect your landscaping.

roofing_notes: Bungalow and Victorian roofs have many valleys, dormers and porch tie-ins; ask how each roofer flashes those joints.
Per its guidelines, re-roofing in the Tazewell Pike conservation district does not need Historic Zoning Commission approval.
Pre-1930 homes may have plank decking and old layers underneath; get decking replacement priced in writing.
Mature shade trees bring moss and clogged gutters; ask about trimming clearance and gutter guards.

faqs.q: Do I need historic approval to replace a roof in Fountain City?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Gibbs Drive is on the National Register, which recognizes its history but does not by itself trigger design review for a private re-roof. The Tazewell Pike Neighborhood Conservation District's guidelines specifically say roofing does not need Historic Zoning Commission approval. Fountain City is inside Knoxville city limits, so ask your roofer whether your job needs a city building permit.

faqs.q: What makes re-roofing an old bungalow different?
faqs.a: Bungalows from the 1910s and 1920s often have low-pitched roofs, wide overhangs, exposed rafter tails and front porches tied into the main roof. Low slopes need careful underlayment, and the porch and dormer joints need solid flashing. Older homes may also have plank decking rather than plywood. Ask each roofer how they would handle those details and how they price decking repairs.

faqs.q: Is Fountain City part of Knoxville?
faqs.a: Yes. Fountain City resisted annexation, but Knoxville took it in 1962, and residents marked the day with a mock funeral procession down Broadway. Today it is a city neighborhood with Knoxville mailing addresses in the 37918 and 37912 ZIP codes, so city rules apply to building work. You can request quotes for any Fountain City address and compare up to three licensed roofers.

name: South Knoxville
title: South Knoxville Roofing Quotes | Compare Local Roofers

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in South Knoxville
hero_subtitle: From Island Home Park bungalows to homes along Chapman Highway and the wooded edges of the Urban Wilderness, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed South Knoxville roofers. Free, no obligation.
intro: South Knoxville is the part of the city across the Tennessee River from downtown. It stayed thinly settled for most of the 1800s because so few bridges crossed the river, and Knoxville annexed parts of it in 1917. Marble quarries, mills and streetcar lines shaped its older neighborhoods, and the Urban Wilderness, about 1,000 acres of parks and preserved land, now gives SoKno a hillier, more wooded setting than most of Knoxville. Request quotes and compare up to three licensed, insured roofers.

sections.heading: Old streetcar neighborhoods by the river
body: Island Home Park began in 1911, when the Island Home Park Company sold its first lot on a 117-acre tract between the river and what became the Tennessee School for the Deaf. Its roughly 200 homes are known for Craftsman bungalows built mostly in the 1910s and 1920s, and the neighborhood was listed on the National Register in 1994. Island Home Boulevard was Knoxville's first designated boulevard.

Nearby, Old Sevier grew up around Sevier Avenue, where breweries and restaurants have revived the commercial strip, and Vestal was home to the Candoro Marble Works. In neighborhoods this old, a roof replacement can uncover plank decking, tired chimney flashing or several layers of earlier roofing that all need to come off.

sections.heading: Hills, quarries and the Urban Wilderness
body: The Urban Wilderness links Ijams Nature Center, Baker Creek Preserve, Fort Dickerson and High Ground Park, with roughly 50 miles of trails across old quarry land and the hilltops where Union troops built forts in 1863. Homes that back up to these woods or sit on the steep streets nearby live with a lot of tree cover.

For a roof, that means leaves and pine needles collecting in valleys and gutters, moss and algae on shaded slopes, and limbs that can come down in a storm. On steep lots, ask how the roofer plans to get materials up to the house and where the dumpster will go.

sections.heading: City or county, and Chapman Highway
body: Not everything called South Knoxville is inside the city. Parts of it, including the area around South-Doyle High School, lie outside Knoxville city limits in unincorporated Knox County. Confirm which applies to your home so your roofer knows which office handles any permit.

Chapman Highway, which opened in 1934 as the Smoky Mountain Highway and was later renamed for national park champion David Chapman, is still being widened in sections. Work between Hendron Chapel Road and Simpson Road is expected to wrap up in 2026. If your home is near a work zone, ask roofers how they will handle crew parking and debris removal.

roofing_notes: Century-old bungalows in Island Home Park may hide plank decking and old flashing; ask for itemized repair pricing.
Homes near the Urban Wilderness get heavy leaf and needle fall; ask about gutter guards and algae-resistant shingles.
On steep streets, ask where the crew will stage materials and park the dumpster.
Confirm whether your address is inside Knoxville city limits or in unincorporated Knox County.

faqs.q: Does Island Home Park's historic status limit my roofing choices?
faqs.a: Island Home Park is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, which honors the neighborhood's history but generally does not require design review for a privately paid re-roof. Local historic zoning is what sets rules where it exists, so before you choose a material, check with Knoxville-Knox County Planning whether any local overlay applies to your lot.

faqs.q: My house backs up to the woods near Ijams. What roof problems should I watch for?
faqs.a: Trees are the big one. Leaves and needles collect in valleys and gutters and hold moisture against shingles, shaded roof faces grow moss and algae, and limbs can fall in storms. Ask roofers about algae-resistant shingles, gutter guards and trimming branches back from the roof. Checking gutters each fall and after storms can catch problems before they reach the decking.

faqs.q: How do I get quotes for a home along Chapman Highway?
faqs.a: Enter your address and a short description of the roof on the form. Up to three licensed, insured roofers who work in South Knoxville can contact you, usually within 24 to 48 hours. If your home is near ongoing Chapman Highway widening, mention it so contractors can plan for access, parking and debris removal. There is no cost and no obligation.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Tellico Village, TN
hero_subtitle: Exterior changes in Tellico Village go through the Architectural Control Committee. Compare up to 3 quotes from licensed roofers before you apply. Free for homeowners, with no obligation.
intro: Tellico Village is a planned lake and golf community on the western shore of Tellico Lake, developed by Cooper Communities starting in 1986. The first residents moved in in 1987, and the village now has more than 7,000 residents, most of them 65 or older. Seven of its eight neighborhoods are in Loudon County, while Kahite sits about 10 miles south in Monroe County near Vonore. Roof work here runs through the property owners association's Architectural Control Committee, which shapes how you plan and price a replacement.

sections.heading: Homes from 1987 to today
body: Cooper Communities took title to the land in December 1985, began selling lots the next year and welcomed the first residents in February 1987. Building has continued since then across Chatuga, Chota, Coyatee, Mialaquo, Tanasi, Tommotley, Toqua and Kahite, so roof ages vary a great deal from one street to the next. The covenants call for at least 1,200 square feet of heated space plus an enclosed two-car garage.

Homes from the village's first decade are now three to four decades old, which is longer than most asphalt shingle roofs last. If you bought here recently, ask the seller or your home inspector when the current roof went on. When roofers visit, ask them to look closely at low-pitch sections and at flashing where decks, porches and sunrooms join the house.

sections.heading: Working with the Architectural Control Committee
body: The Tellico Village POA handbook is direct: building any structure or changing a home's exterior requires a permit, and even repainting a house the same color needs a no-charge permit. The Architectural Control Committee meets on the first and third Thursdays of each month, and color chips and samples are required with applications.

Roof color is where most of the rules apply. The POA favors neutral, soft tones, and its handbook states that no colorful, shiny or reflective roofs, metallic or otherwise, are permitted. That does not rule out every metal product; a stone-coated steel roofing system appeared on the committee's November 2025 agenda, for example. Ask your roofer for the exact product name, color and samples to submit, and do not schedule work until the permit is approved.

sections.heading: Lake wind, wooded lots and timing
body: The village sits on rolling, wooded hills beside a reservoir of roughly 16,000 acres. Lakefront and golf course homes are more open to wind, while homes on wooded lots collect leaves and needles in roof valleys and gutters.

Plan around the permit calendar and the weather. Workers are generally allowed on site Monday through Saturday, and the POA notes that roofers often work the cooler hours of the day. If you spend part of the year elsewhere, arrange for someone nearby to meet the roofer and look over the finished job.

roofing_notes: Get Architectural Control Committee approval before any re-roof; changing a home's exterior requires a POA permit.
Choose neutral, soft-toned roofing; the POA does not permit colorful, shiny or reflective roofs.
Bring exact product names, color chips and samples to the ACC application.
Kahite is in Monroe County, where code inspections have been handled by TRDA rather than Loudon County.

faqs.q: Do I need ACC approval to replace my roof in Tellico Village?

faqs.q: Can I put a metal roof on my Tellico Village home?
faqs.a: Possibly, but appearance is the test. The POA does not permit colorful, shiny or reflective roofs, metallic or otherwise, and it favors neutral, soft tones. Low-sheen products such as stone-coated steel have come before the committee, including on its November 2025 agenda. Ask roofers for the exact product and color, and get ACC approval before ordering materials.
